case_title: Deep Narayan Chourasia v. State of Bihar
aggravating_circumstances: Formation of unlawful assembly, firing in the air to threaten villagers
trial_court_outcome: Accused Kanhai Prasad Chourasia convicted under s.302 IPC and s.27 Arms Act; other four acquitted under s.149 IPC but convicted under s.27 Arms Act
high_court_outcome: Convicted four co-accused under s.302/149 IPC along with Kanhai Prasad Chourasia
neutral_facts: The accused, five individuals, were tried for the murder of a woman. The trial court acquitted four of them of murder but convicted them under the Arms Act. The High Court, however, incorrectly convicted all five under murder charges without proper appeal or evidence. The Supreme Court found the High Court's judgment flawed and set it aside, remanding the case for re-hearing. The evidence included witness accounts and a record of events, suggesting the accused formed an unlawful assembly and used firearms, leading to the victim's death. The trial court's acquittal of the four accused under Section 149 IPC was not challenged by the State, yet the High Court proceeded to convict them under Section 302/149 IPC without justification.
